rationale: design-import-refactor: generic change landed in Pulp per owner decision 2026-10-04; Vellum inherits (see inheritance ledger); the ImageFileCache path pool was bounded only by entry count, so its 32 entries could pin over a gigabyte of decoded pixels or textures, and a build that returned null (a missing file, a corrupt data: URI) was retried on every lookup, decoding a broken asset on every paint. The path pool now also has a 64 MiB byte budget with LRU eviction (set_byte_budget, Stats.bytes) and keeps its newest entry even when that one image exceeds the budget, so a large backdrop is decoded once rather than every frame; the inline pool's build-uncached rule is unchanged. Both pools remember a failed build for one second, and clear()/clear_backend() drop those records. Pixel output is unchanged. No design-import, Chromium, rendering, packaging, or source-authority boundary moves.
tests: ctest --test-dir build -R 'A failed build is remembered for the retry window'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'File pool keeps a lone image larger than its byte budget'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'File pool stays within its byte budget'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'ImageFileCache: null build result is not stored'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'Inline pool still builds an over-budget image uncached'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'clear_backend drops only that backend.s failure records'
